title: Explain emergency preparedness and response procedures

lessons.title: Types of emergencies on a farm
lessons.html:
What is an emergency?

An emergency is a sudden event that puts people, animals, property or the environment in danger and needs fast action. Every farm, packhouse and abattoir must plan for emergencies. The Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 requires employers to provide a safe workplace, and an emergency plan is part of that.

Emergencies you may face

TypeFarm examples
FireVeld fire, fire in a hay store, workshop or packhouse, electrical fire
ChemicalSpill of pesticide or diesel, ammonia leak from a cold store, poisoning
MedicalSerious injury from a tractor or machine, snake bite, heat stroke, heart attack
NaturalFlood, lightning, storm, hail
StructuralCollapse of a shed, silo or dam wall
AnimalCharging bull, stampede, outbreak of a controlled animal disease
SecurityArmed robbery, farm attack, stock theft in progress
TransportBakkie or tractor rollover, truck accident on the farm road

Why preparation matters

In an emergency there is no time to think. People who know what to do, where to go and who to call act faster and save lives. That is why farms have emergency plans, alarms, assembly points, trained first aiders and fire fighters, and regular drills.

Know your farm

  • Where are the fire extinguishers, hoses and fire beaters?
  • Where is the first aid box?
  • Where are the exits and the assembly point?
  • What are the emergency numbers, and where are they displayed?

lessons.title: Responding to an alarm
lessons.html:
Types of alarms

Workplaces use different alarms: a siren, a bell, a hooter, a gong, a whistle, or a message on the radio or phone. Each workplace decides what each signal means, for example one long siren for fire and evacuation, or short blasts for a chemical leak. Learn your workplace's signals during induction.

When you hear the evacuation alarm

  1. Stop work immediately. Switch off machines if it is safe and quick to do so.
  2. Do not stop to collect personal belongings.
  3. Leave by the nearest safe exit. Walk quickly; do not run or push.
  4. Help visitors and people who need help, if you can do so safely.
  5. Do not use lifts in buildings that have them.
  6. Go to the assembly point and report to the person taking the roll call.
  7. Stay at the assembly point until you are told it is safe to return.

Different responses

  • Fire: raise the alarm. Fight a small fire only if you are trained, have the right extinguisher and have an escape route behind you. Stay low under smoke.
  • Chemical or gas leak: move away and upwind. Do not try to stop the leak unless trained and equipped.
  • Storm or lightning: get inside a building or vehicle. Stay away from tractors in open fields, wire fences and lone trees.
  • Security threat: follow the farm's security plan. Do not resist armed attackers. Call for help when it is safe.

Never

  • Never ignore an alarm, thinking it is a drill.
  • Never go back into a building for belongings.
  • Never re-enter until the person in charge says it is safe.

lessons.title: The assembly area and the emergency control centre
lessons.html:
The safety officer at the assembly area

The assembly area (assembly point) is a safe, open place away from buildings, marked with a sign. A safety officer, marshal or supervisor is in charge there. Their actions include:

  1. Take the roll call: check everyone against the clock-in register, staff list and visitor book.
  2. Report missing people to the emergency controller at once, with their names and last known location.
  3. Keep people together and calm; stop anyone from going back.
  4. Check for injured people and call first aiders.
  5. Pass on information from the emergency control centre, and give the all-clear only when instructed.
  6. Record what happened for the incident report.

Search and rescue is done by trained people only. Never send untrained workers into danger to look for someone.

The emergency control centre

On a large farm or in a packhouse or abattoir, an emergency control centre is a set place, such as the farm office or security gate, from where the emergency is managed. Its functions:

  • Receive the alarm and decide on the response.
  • Call outside services: fire brigade, ambulance, police, municipal disaster management, poison information.
  • Direct the farm's own teams: fire fighters, first aiders, security.
  • Keep contact with assembly points and get roll call results.
  • Meet and guide outside services to the scene.
  • Keep a log of events, times and decisions.
  • Inform management and, when needed, neighbours, for example of a veld fire.

The centre should have a list of emergency numbers, a site map, radios or phones, the staff list, first aid equipment and torches.

Key points

  • Emergencies include fire, chemical, medical, natural, animal and security events.
  • Learn your workplace's alarm signals and the nearest exits.
  • On the alarm: stop, leave by the nearest safe exit, go to the assembly point, stay there.
  • The safety officer takes the roll call and reports missing people at once.
  • The emergency control centre coordinates the response and calls outside services.

quiz.question: You hear the evacuation alarm. What should you do first?

options.text: Stop work and leave by the nearest safe exit
Wait to see if it is a drill

quiz.question: Which is the main job of the safety officer at the assembly area?

options.text: To take a roll call and report missing people

quiz.question: There is an ammonia leak from a cold store. Where should you move?

options.text: Towards the leak to see it

quiz.question: Which is a function of the emergency control centre?

options.text: Calling outside services such as the fire brigade and ambulance

quiz.question: When may you fight a small fire?

options.text: Only if trained, with the right extinguisher and an escape route behind you
Always, even if the fire is large
Only if no one is watching

quiz.question: During a lightning storm, you should shelter under a lone tree in the field.
You must stay at the assembly point until you are told it is safe to return.
Which items should be available at the emergency control centre? (select all that apply)
